question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund is a close-ended Category III AIF (NOT an LVF) with investable funds of INR 600 crore. What is the maximum concentration limit in a single investee company?

answer.text: INR 60 crore (10% of investable funds — general Cat III cap)
INR 120 crore (20% of investable funds — LVF cap)
INR 150 crore (25% of investable funds — Cat I/II close-ended cap)
INR 60 crore (10% — same for open-ended and close-ended Cat III)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, Category III AIFs — whether open-ended or close-ended — are capped at 10% of investable funds in a single investee company. Thus 10% × INR 600 cr = INR 60 crore. The 20% concession applies ONLY to LVFs of Cat III; Cat I/II close-ended have 25%. The Trap: Options A and D are both INR 60 cr — the difference is the REASONING. A asserts open-ended only; correct answer D clarifies the 10% applies irrespective of open/close. B is LVF-only; C is Cat I/II. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests Cat I/II close-ended 25%. XIX-C tests both. XIX-E locks on the unified 10% Cat III cap. Manager's Pro-Tip: When sizing a merger-arb or special-situation position, the 10% cap against investable funds is binding. LVF conversion unlocks 20% but the AI-only consent and INR 25 cr minimum-per-investor rules apply.
